public.title: homelab
public.description: A geo-distributed, GitOps-managed K3s cluster spanning Florida and Medellín, Colombia over Tailscale. Every change goes through a pull request and Argo CD; nothing is applied by hand.
features: Six-node cluster (3-member etcd control plane plus amd64 GPU and arm64 workers) across two countries, joined over Tailscale with Cilium native routing and no kube-proxy
~90 Argo CD Applications via App of Apps with directory auto-discovery and ApplicationSets
PR gate on every manifest change: yamllint, kubeconform, and a full Argo CD render of both branches in an ephemeral cluster, posted back as a diff comment

Four independent backup layers to self-hosted Garage S3: VolSync/restic PVC snapshots with an hourly end-to-end restore canary, CNPG continuous WAL archiving (14-day PITR), etcd snapshots every 6h, and an off-host copy of Garage itself
Observability on kube-prometheus-stack with Thanos and Loki shipping long-term data to S3, plus OpenTelemetry
Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners (ARC) split by CPU architecture; Ansible runs keyless from CI over Tailscale SSH with 1Password-sourced secrets
Secrets from 1Password Operator, Tailscale ACLs as code, UPS-driven graceful shutdown via NUT, and written postmortems for real outages

public.title: juanflix
public.description: The community portal for my Plex servers. It manages who has access (invites, library shares, removals), shows activity, and lets maintainers add and search titles across Sonarr and Radarr, with an editable roles-and-permissions model behind every action.
features: Two sign-in paths: OIDC for admins and Plex accounts for friends, with audited access changes
Built-in MCP server with its own OAuth authorization server, so Claude can add titles and file Seerr requests under the user's own permissions
Cleanup report from Tautulli and Seerr that flags titles nobody watches, without ever deleting media
Structured JSON logs with secret redaction, plus Prometheus metrics for scheduled jobs and upstream API health

public.title: herald
public.description: A Cloudflare-native push notification server and companion iOS app that replaced a self-hosted ntfy, so alerts still reach my phone when the cluster itself is down.
features: Accepts Alertmanager and apprise publishes and fans out through Cloudflare Queues to APNs, with a dead-letter queue and per-device delivery log
Pairs with the status page so a stale cluster heartbeat pages with zero homelab components in the path
iOS app with an inbox that keeps missed or dismissed pushes, built and shipped to TestFlight from GitHub Actions
Preact admin console and OIDC sign-in through wisp

public.title: wisp
public.description: My own OpenID Connect identity provider, running as a single Cloudflare Worker. It is the SSO for the whole homelab and replaced a self-hosted IdP.
features: Authorization Code + PKCE for Grafana, Argo CD, Immich, oauth2-proxy and my own apps
Separate dev and prod environments; client secrets delivered straight into 1Password

public.title: status page
public.description: A public status page that watches the homelab from outside it, on Cloudflare Workers, with an in-cluster companion that sends heartbeats and relays Alertmanager alerts.
features: Detects a dead cluster from the outside and pages through herald
90-day uptime rollups computed incrementally to keep Cloudflare usage low

public.title: homelab-mcp
public.description: An MCP server that exposes the media-automation stack (Seerr, Radarr, Sonarr, qBittorrent, SABnzbd, Tautulli) as tools, so an AI client can operate it without shell access to the cluster.
features: Stateless HTTP transport with auth, deployed in-cluster
Multi-arch (amd64 + arm64) images published to GHCR on tagged releases

public.title: resume
public.description: this resume is defined in github and deployed through github actions to a static site hosted on my homelab. The resume is built using React and Tailwind CSS, and the content is managed through JSON files.
features: Static site deployment
Responsive design
Content management through JSON
Leverages CI/CD (github actions) for automated lint, build, test and deploy
Dockerized for easy deployment

public.title: git2jamf
public.description: A github action that synchronizes Git repositories with Jamf Pro, streamlining the deployment of scripts and configurations and allowing for version control missing in JAMF.
features: Automated synchronization between Git repositories and Jamf Pro
Git triggers for real-time updates
Comprehensive logging and error handling
Docker containerization for easy deployment

work.title: Metrics and Monitoring
work.description: Implemented Grafana's mimir along with grafana itself on AWS EKS for metrics storage and monitoring, enhancing observability and creating a centralized dashboard for all cluster and services. I secured the remote write endpoints using auth2proxy allowing for m2m authentication with the prometheus clients and getting us off mainting whitelists and security groups
features: Centralized metrics dashboard
Enhanced observability
Real-time monitoring
Scalable architecture
oauth2proxy Machine to machine authentication

work.title: Custom Metrics Exporter
work.description: Wrote a custom metric's exporter for Scuba's services to expose metrics that were not natively generated  by the application. This allows for better monitoring and alerting on critical application metrics.
features: Custom metrics collection
Prometheus compatible exporter
Lightweight fastapi endpoint that generates metrics on scrape
Alerting on critical application metrics

work.title: OSS Inventory - SnipeIT
work.description: Implemented the first inventory system for Sonos's IT assets, including hardware and software, using SnipeIT. This system allows for better tracking and management of IT resources, ensuring compliance and optimizing asset utilization. Offered it as a service to other teams in the org.
features: Centralized asset management
Integrated with existing systems (jamf, intune, sccm) to automatically add and track assets
Automated inventory updates

work.title: Incident Management for IT
work.description: Created a workflow through the use of aws lambda, python and the API's of the various services we used (pagerduty, jira, confluence, slack) to create an Incident Mangement system for IT that handled the entire lifecycle of an incident from creation to resolution. This system allowed for better tracking and management of incidents, improving response times and reducing downtime.
features: Automated incident lifecycle management
Integration with existing tools (pagerduty, jira, confluence, slack)
Improved response times and reduced downtime
